title: C-REACTIVE PROTEIN IS A POWERFUL MARKER OF SELF-RATED HEALTH AMONG CHINESE OLDER ADULTS
abstract:
R Yang, Y Liu, T Liu, C Li, C-REACTIVE PROTEIN IS A POWERFUL MARKER OF SELF-RATED HEALTH AMONG CHINESE OLDER ADULTS,
*Innovation in Aging*, Volume 2, Issue suppl_1, November 2018, Page 706, https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igy023.2620
...
Using a nationally representative sample of older adults who are 65 years and older (N = 2,694) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we examined the association between C-reactive protein (CRP) and the single-item SRH.
...
The findings showed that after controlling for age, gender, and BMI, hs-CRP was associated with 0.03 (in 3 units of hs-CRP) lower SRH (95% CI = -0.04, -0.01; p = 0.001).
When further controlling for education, marital status, smoking, drinking, medication use, comorbidity, and depression, the association remained significant (in 3 units of hs-CRP: b = -0.03; 95% CI = -0.03, -0.00; p = 0.025).
The same patterns of findings were replicated in ordinal logistic regression treating the same outcome as an ordinal variable.
The findings suggested that hs-CRP plays a significant role in older adults’ perceptions of general health status, and CRP can be used as an objective marker of SRH among Chinese older adults.
